  "claims": [
    {
      "id": "f1",
      "concept_id": "c2",
      "text": "A checkpoint transfers transactions from the WAL file back into the database.",
      "source_id": "S1",
      "quote": "Moving the WAL file transactions back into the database is called a \" checkpoint \".",
      "pass": 0
    },
    {
      "id": "f2",
      "concept_id": "c3",
      "text": "SQLite's default automatic checkpoint threshold is 1000 WAL pages.",
      "source_id": "S1",
      "quote": "By default, SQLite does a checkpoint automatically when the WAL file reaches a threshold size of 1000 pages.",
      "pass": 0
    },
    {
      "id": "f3",
      "concept_id": "c3",
      "text": "An automatic checkpoint is triggered when a COMMIT makes the WAL at least 1000 pages long.",
      "source_id": "S1",
      "quote": "whenever a COMMIT occurs that causes the WAL file to be 1000 pages or more in size",
      "pass": 0
    },
    {
      "id": "f4",
      "concept_id": "c3",
      "text": "SQLite also checkpoints when the last connection to a database file closes.",
      "source_id": "S1",
      "quote": "By default, SQLite will automatically checkpoint whenever a COMMIT occurs that causes the WAL file to be 1000 pages or more in size, or when the last database connection on a database file closes.",
      "pass": 0
    },
    {
      "id": "f5",
      "concept_id": "c4",
      "text": "sqlite3_wal_autocheckpoint sets a frame threshold that triggers a checkpoint after a transaction commits.",
      "source_id": "S3",
      "quote": "causes any database on database connection D to automatically checkpoint after committing a transaction if there are N or more frames in the write-ahead log file.",
      "pass": 0
    },
    {
      "id": "f6",
      "concept_id": "c4",
      "text": "Passing zero or a negative N to sqlite3_wal_autocheckpoint disables automatic checkpoints.",
      "source_id": "S3",
      "quote": "Passing zero or a negative value as the N parameter disables automatic checkpoints entirely.",
      "pass": 0
    },
    {
      "id": "f7",
      "concept_id": "c4",
      "text": "sqlite3_wal_autocheckpoint replaces an existing WAL hook, and registering a WAL hook disables its automatic checkpoint mechanism.",
      "source_id": "S3",
      "quote": "The callback registered by this function replaces any existing callback registered using sqlite3_wal_hook() . Likewise, registering a callback using sqlite3_wal_hook() disables the automatic checkpoint mechanism configured by this function.",
      "pass": 0
    },
    {
      "id": "f8",
      "concept_id": "c4",
      "text": "Automatic checkpoints use PASSIVE mode.",
      "source_id": "S1",
      "quote": "All checkpoints initiated by sqlite3_wal_checkpoint() and by the automatic checkpoint mechanism are PASSIVE.",
      "pass": 0
    },
    {
      "id": "f9",
      "concept_id": "c5",
      "text": "An application can initiate a checkpoint with the wal_checkpoint pragma or sqlite3_wal_checkpoint().",
      "source_id": "S1",
      "quote": "programs that want more control can force a checkpoint using the wal_checkpoint pragma or by calling the sqlite3_wal_checkpoint() C interface.",
      "pass": 0
    },
    {
      "id": "f10",
      "concept_id": "c6",
      "text": "PASSIVE checkpoints as many frames as possible without waiting for readers or writers and syncs the database only if all log frames were checkpointed.",
      "source_id": "S2",
      "quote": "Checkpoint as many frames as possible without waiting for any database readers or writers to finish, then sync the database file if all frames in the log were checkpointed.",
      "pass": 0
    },
    {
      "id": "f11",
      "concept_id": "c6",
      "text": "PASSIVE may leave a checkpoint unfinished when readers or writers are concurrent.",
      "source_id": "S2",
      "quote": "On the other hand, passive mode might leave the checkpoint unfinished if there are concurrent readers or writers.",
      "pass": 0
    },
    {
      "id": "f12",
      "concept_id": "c6",
      "text": "PASSIVE never invokes the busy-handler callback.",
      "source_id": "S2",
      "quote": "then sync the database file if all frames in the log were checkpointed. The busy-handler callback is never invoked in the SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_PASSIVE mode.",
      "pass": 0
    },
    {
      "id": "f13",
      "concept_id": "c7",
      "text": "FULL waits until there is no database writer and all readers use the most recent snapshot, then checkpoints all log frames and syncs the database.",
      "source_id": "S2",
      "quote": "This mode blocks (it invokes the busy-handler callback ) until there is no database writer and all readers are reading from the most recent database snapshot. It then checkpoints all frames in the log file and syncs the database file.",
      "pass": 0
    },
    {
      "id": "f14",
      "concept_id": "c7",
      "text": "FULL blocks new database writers while pending but allows new readers to continue.",
      "source_id": "S2",
      "quote": "This mode blocks new database writers while it is pending, but new database readers are allowed to continue unimpeded.",
      "pass": 0
    },
    {
      "id": "f15",
      "concept_id": "c8",
      "text": "RESTART waits until all readers use only the database file, so the next writer can restart the log from its beginning.",
      "source_id": "S2",
      "quote": "after checkpointing the log file it blocks (calls the busy-handler callback ) until all readers are reading from the database file only. This ensures that the next writer will restart the log file from the beginning.",
      "pass": 0
    },
    {
      "id": "f16",
      "concept_id": "c9",
      "text": "TRUNCATE performs RESTART behavior and truncates the log to zero bytes before successful return.",
      "source_id": "S2",
      "quote": "This mode works the same way as SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_RESTART with the addition that it also truncates the log file to zero bytes just prior to a successful return.",
      "pass": 0
    },
    {
      "id": "f17",
      "concept_id": "c10",
      "text": "NOOP checkpoints zero frames.",
      "source_id": "S2",
      "quote": "This mode always checkpoints zero frames. The only reason to invoke a NOOP checkpoint is to access the values returned by sqlite3_wal_checkpoint_v2() via output parameters *pnLog and *pnCkpt.",
      "pass": 0
    },
    {
      "id": "f18",
      "concept_id": "c10",
      "text": "The documented purpose of NOOP is to retrieve sqlite3_wal_checkpoint_v2 output values.",
      "source_id": "S2",
      "quote": "The only reason to invoke a NOOP checkpoint is to access the values returned by sqlite3_wal_checkpoint_v2() via output parameters *pnLog and *pnCkpt.",
      "pass": 0
    },
    {
      "id": "f19",
      "concept_id": "c11",
      "text": "A concurrent checkpoint can prevent acquisition of the exclusive checkpoint lock, causing SQLITE_BUSY.",
      "source_id": "S2",
      "quote": "All calls obtain an exclusive \"checkpoint\" lock on the database file. If any other process is running a checkpoint operation at the same time, the lock cannot be obtained and SQLITE_BUSY is returned.",
      "pass": 0
    },
    {
      "id": "f20",
      "concept_id": "c11",
      "text": "FULL, RESTART, and TRUNCATE also obtain the exclusive writer lock.",
      "source_id": "S2",
      "quote": "The SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_FULL, RESTART and TRUNCATE modes also obtain the exclusive \"writer\" lock on the database file.",
      "pass": 0
    },
    {
      "id": "f21",
      "concept_id": "c11",
      "text": "If the busy handler returns zero while acquiring the writer lock or waiting for readers, the checkpoint proceeds in PASSIVE-like fashion.",
      "source_id": "S2",
      "quote": "If the busy-handler returns 0 before the writer lock is obtained or while waiting for database readers, the checkpoint operation proceeds from that point in the same way as SQLITE_CHECKPOINT_PASSIVE",
      "pass": 0
    },
    {
      "id": "f22",
      "concept_id": "c11",
      "text": "That fallback checkpoints without further blocking and returns SQLITE_BUSY.",
      "source_id": "S2",
      "quote": "checkpointing as many frames as possible without blocking any further. SQLITE_BUSY is returned in this case.",
      "pass": 0
    },
    {
      "id": "f23",
      "concept_id": "c12",
      "text": "A checkpoint stops at a WAL page past a current reader's end mark because continuing could overwrite database content that reader is using.",
      "source_id": "S1",
      "quote": "past the end mark of any current reader. The checkpoint has to stop at that point because otherwise it might overwrite part of the database file that the reader is actively using.",
      "pass": 0
    },
    {
      "id": "f24",
      "concept_id": "c12",
      "text": "The checkpointer records its progress in the wal-index and resumes from that point on the next invocation.",
      "source_id": "S1",
      "quote": "The checkpoint remembers (in the wal-index) how far it got and will resume transferring content from the WAL to the database from where it left off on the next invocation.",
      "pass": 0
    },
    {
      "id": "f25",
      "concept_id": "c12",
      "text": "A long-running read transaction can prevent a checkpointer from making progress.",
      "source_id": "S1",
      "quote": "Thus a long-running read transaction can prevent a checkpointer from making progress.",
      "pass": 0
    },
    {
      "id": "f26",
      "concept_id": "c13",
      "text": "If overlapping readers ensure at least one reader is always active, checkpoints cannot complete and the WAL can grow without bound.",
      "source_id": "S1",
      "quote": "if a database has many concurrent overlapping readers and there is always at least one active reader, then no checkpoints will be able to complete and hence the WAL file will grow without bound.",
      "pass": 0
    },
    {
      "id": "f27",
      "concept_id": "c13",
      "text": "SQLite recommends attempting checkpoints during reader gaps when no processes are reading.",
      "source_id": "S1",
      "quote": "This scenario can be avoided by ensuring that there are \"reader gaps\": times when no processes are reading from the database and that checkpoints are attempted during those times.",
      "pass": 0
    },
    {
      "id": "f28",
      "concept_id": "c14",
      "text": "A checkpoint normally reuses the WAL by overwriting it from the beginning instead of truncating it, unless journal_size_limit is set.",
      "source_id": "S1",
      "quote": "The checkpoint does not normally truncate the WAL file (unless the journal_size_limit pragma is set). Instead, it merely causes SQLite to start overwriting the WAL file from the beginning.",
      "pass": 0
    },
    {
      "id": "f29",
      "concept_id": "c14",
      "text": "A writer rewinds the WAL only after all WAL content is transferred and synced and no readers are using it.",
      "source_id": "S1",
      "quote": "if the entire WAL has been transferred into the database and synced and if no readers are making use of the WAL, then the writer will rewind the WAL back to the beginning",
      "pass": 0
    },
    {
      "id": "f30",
      "concept_id": "c14",
      "text": "When the last connection closes, SQLite checkpoints once and deletes the WAL and its shared-memory file.",
      "source_id": "S1",
      "quote": "When the last connection to a database closes, that connection does one last checkpoint and then deletes the WAL and its associated shared-memory file, to clean up the disk.",
      "pass": 0
    },
    {
      "id": "f31",
      "concept_id": "c15",
      "text": "Time spent checking the WAL for reader content is proportional to WAL file size.",
      "source_id": "S1",
      "quote": "the time needed to check the WAL file is proportional to the size of the WAL file.",
      "pass": 0
    },
    {
      "id": "f32",
      "concept_id": "c15",
      "text": "Regular checkpoints keep the WAL small to maintain good read performance.",
      "source_id": "S1",
      "quote": "Hence, to maintain good read performance it is important to keep the WAL file size down by running checkpoints at regular intervals.",
      "pass": 0
    },
    {
      "id": "f33",
      "concept_id": "c15",
      "text": "Checkpoint frequency trades off average read performance against average write performance.",
      "source_id": "S1",
      "quote": "Notice too that there is a tradeoff between average read performance and average write performance.",
      "pass": 0
    },
    {
      "id": "f34",
      "concept_id": "c15",
      "text": "Seek operations interspersed among page writes contribute to checkpoints being slower than write transactions.",
      "source_id": "S1",
      "quote": "there will typically be many seek operations interspersed among the page writes. These factors combine to make checkpoints slower than write transactions.",
      "pass": 0
    },
    {
      "id": "f35",
      "concept_id": "c16",
      "text": "SQLite syncs the WAL before moving its content into the database, then syncs the database before resetting the WAL.",
      "source_id": "S1",
      "quote": "The WAL must be synced to persistent storage prior to moving content from the WAL into the database and the database file must be synced prior to resetting the WAL.",
      "pass": 0
    },
    {
      "id": "f36",
      "concept_id": "c16",
      "text": "With PRAGMA synchronous=NORMAL, checkpointing is the only operation that issues an I/O barrier or sync operation.",
      "source_id": "S1",
      "quote": "with PRAGMA synchronous set to NORMAL, the checkpoint is the only operation to issue an I/O barrier or sync operation (fsync() on unix or FlushFileBuffers() on windows).",
      "pass": 0
    }
  ],
  "passes": [
    {
      "pass": 0,
      "new_claims": 36,
      "total_claims": 36,
      "new_information_rate": 1.0
    }
  ],
  "handoffs": [],
  "verdict": "BOUNDED-STAGE",
  "limitations": [
    "Evidence is limited to three supplied pages on sqlite.org; independent-origin corroboration was not supplied.",
    "S1's subtype summary names PASSIVE, FULL, and RESTART; S2 gives fuller API definitions and additionally defines TRUNCATE and NOOP. The packet gives no history for this difference, so detailed mode claims follow S2.",
    "The packet contains no history of disagreements beyond this documentation-scope difference."
  ]
}
